author: mettafort
text:
If I were a song...http://m.youtube.com/watch?v=ov9kH54Z- dM&desktop_uri=%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dov9kH54Z-dM OK got it. I did know that actually, but for some reason applied it incorrectly.

With respect to that trade that you took. I can see how one PA component led to another, and while it all looks like chaos at the point of your entry, it was simply the final alignment of PA that sealed the trade.

One but I am not sure about, is where you actually entered. I see in that choppiness, higher highs - engulfs - and then pullbacks. But did you wait till that final engulf which takes out the high on the left of that choppiness, or were you in actually sooner? That is, was the fakeout the crucial piece before getting ready to hit fire?

Thanks again, MF

author: Kruger
text: Waiting for engulf is very wise thing but in this case I took long bit earlier.

I know I have learnt a lot from both. This is not a journey for the ego, that I know, so it is useful to be reminded of that very important point lest I forget it to my chagrin.

Thank you, MF

Hi Fxyogi, yes, from 'touch' (order consumption) perspective S/R and supp/dem are similar, we should always expect many orders in both directions.

I consider S/R as kind of a border separating two opposing forces.
